budget: What is a financial safety cushion?
A reserve of money for unexpected expenses
A deposit that cannot be withdrawn
It is used when something goes wrong.
A cushion is an easily accessible reserve in case of job loss, illness or a breakdown. It is usually advised to keep 3–6 months of expenses.
What size of safety cushion is usually recommended?
The cost of one big purchase
It is counted in months of living.
3–6 months of essential expenses is enough to survive a job loss and calmly find a new one.
A plan of income and expenses for a period
The amount on a bank card
It is a plan, not a balance.
A budget compares expected income and expenses so you know in advance whether the money will be enough and how much you can save.
First repay all loans in full
First set aside part of your income, then spend
Pay yourself a bonus from savings
Saving right after you get paid is more reliable than saving whatever is left at the end of the month: often nothing is left.
Those you cannot do without: housing, food, transport
Essential expenses are the base of a budget. They are covered first, and wants get what remains after them and savings.
A purchase from a prepared list
An unplanned purchase driven by emotions
Emotions are faster than the plan.
Impulse purchases are made because of a discount, an ad or a mood. A pause helps: postpone the decision for a day.
A 24-hour rule before a non-essential purchase
Keeping all money in cash at home
A pause before buying cools emotions. Many things no longer seem necessary a day later.
To see where the money goes
So the bank gives you a loan
You cannot manage what you cannot see.
Tracking shows the real structure of spending: usually there are items you can cut without lowering your quality of life.
Only the amount in your account
The difference between price and discount
All inflows: salary, side jobs, interest
Income is any money received over a period. In a budget it is compared with expenses to see how much is left.
What is it called when expenses exceed income?
A deficit means you spend more than you earn, and savings or debts cover the gap. A surplus is the opposite.
The 50/30/20 rule suggests dividing income like this:
Half of income goes to essentials, 30% to wants, 20% to savings and early debt repayment. It is a guideline, not a law.
Income is 60,000 ₽. How much to save under the 50/30/20 rule?
Where is it best to keep a safety cushion?
In a savings account or deposit that allows withdrawals
A cushion must be accessible and reliable. Shares and crypto can fall in value exactly when you need the money.
What does inflation do to your savings?
Makes the bank charge a fee
Think about what you can buy with them.
If prices rise 8% a year, in a year 100,000 ₽ will buy about as much as 92,600 ₽ today. So money should earn interest no lower than inflation.
Five subscriptions at 299 ₽ a month. How much is that per year?
First the month, then multiply by 12.
5 × 299 = 1,495 ₽ a month, × 12 = 17,940 ₽ a year. Small regular payments add up to a noticeable sum.
The envelope method in budgeting is…
Keeping savings in a bank safe box
Splitting money into categories in advance and staying within the limits
Each category has its own limit.
Each category gets its own envelope, real or virtual. When the envelope is empty, spending in that category stops until the end of the month.
Which goal follows the SMART principle?
Save 150,000 ₽ for a vacation by June by putting aside 15,000 ₽ a month
SMART means specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound. "I want more money" has none of that.
An item costs 10,000 ₽, prices rise 10% a year, a deposit pays 6%. If you need the item, what is better?
Save for a year, a deposit is always better
Compare price growth and deposit growth.
In a year the item will cost 11,000 ₽, and 10,000 ₽ on deposit will become 10,600 ₽. Waiting does not pay, but only if you buy with your own money, without a loan.
What share of income is reasonable to spend on all loan payments?
Any, if you pay on time
You need a buffer for surprises.
With a load above 30–40%, any setback such as illness or a pay cut leads to missed payments.
How does a savings account differ from a term deposit?
Money can be withdrawn at any time without losing interest
A savings account can be topped up and withdrawn from at any time. The price of flexibility is usually a slightly lower rate, which the bank can change.
Small regular expenses that quietly eat up the budget
A 250 ₽ coffee every working day is about 5,500 ₽ a month and 66,000 ₽ a year. You do not have to give it up, just do it consciously.
To save 120,000 ₽ in 10 months, you need to set aside per month:
Divide the goal by the term.
120,000 / 10 = 12,000 ₽ a month. In an interest-bearing account the contribution can be a little smaller.
You save 10,000 ₽ a month without interest, inflation is 10% a year. Roughly what will the savings be worth in a year in today's prices?
On average, contributions sit for half a year.
Nominally it will be 120,000 ₽, but prices will rise meanwhile. Contributions sit for half a year on average and lose about 5%, so in today's money it is about 114,000 ₽.
A pay cut due to inflation
The salary grew, savings did not.
Income grew and spending grew just as much, while savings did not increase. A rule helps: save at least half of every raise.
You have credit card debt at 30% and 50,000 ₽ of free money with no cushion. What is wiser first?
Repay the debt, keeping a small reserve
Repaying a 30% debt is like getting a guaranteed 30% return. But keep a small reserve so you do not go into the red again.
How does "net" income differ from "gross" income?
Net is after taxes and deductions
Gross salary is before tax is withheld, net is what arrives on your card. A budget is planned from the net amount.
Which option is an example of "bad" debt?
A loan to study an in-demand profession
A 0% installment plan for a needed item within budget
A vacation loan at 25% a year
What will bring no benefit in the future?
Expensive debt for consumption that will not pay off is bad. A mortgage or education can pay off, a vacation cannot.
The "snowball" method of paying off debts is…
Pay off the smallest debt first, then the next
Pay off the most expensive debt first
Take a new loan to pay the old one
Pay only the minimum on all debts
Closing small debts quickly gives a sense of progress. Mathematically the "avalanche" is better, highest rate first, but the "snowball" helps you not give up.
Which indicator better reflects financial health?
Net worth: all property minus all debts
A high salary with big debts can mean zero net worth. That is why the rank in the game is based on assets, not cash.
Saving 5,000 ₽ a month at 10% a year with monthly compounding. Roughly how much after 10 years?
Contributions are 600 thousand, interest does the rest.
Contributions alone are 600,000 ₽, and compound interest adds about 420,000 ₽ more: roughly 1.02 million ₽ in total.
banks: How does a debit card differ from a credit card?
A debit card holds your money, a credit card holds the bank's money
A debit card works only online
A credit card cannot be used in shops
No difference, they are the same
Whose money is on the card?
A debit card is linked to your account. A credit card is a bank loan with a limit that must be repaid, often with interest.
Three digits on the back of the card for online payments
It is printed on the back.
CVC/CVV confirms online payments. Never share it with anyone, even a "bank employee".
A refund of part of the purchase amount
The bank returns 1–5% of purchases, sometimes more in selected categories. But cashback is no reason to spend more.
A secret code to confirm card transactions
Do not keep the PIN next to the card or tell it to anyone. Bank employees never ask for it.
What is a deposit interest rate?
A fee for opening a deposit
The income the bank pays you, in percent per year
A rate of 10% a year means the bank will add about 10,000 ₽ per year on 100,000 ₽.
Your card was stolen or lost. What should you do?
Wait, maybe it will turn up
Post about it on social media
Block it right away in the app or via the bank's phone number
The sooner the card is blocked, the smaller the chance someone uses it. The bank's number is on the back of the card and on its website.
A charge for a bank service
A bonus for opening an account
Fees can be for maintenance, transfers, cash withdrawals. Check them in the tariffs before signing up for a product.
A transfer between your own accounts
The ability to go negative on an account within a limit
An overdraft is a short loan tied to a debit card. It is usually expensive, so better not use it unless necessary.
Whom does the deposit insurance system protect?
It is about people's bank deposits.
If a member bank loses its license, deposits are returned up to the set limit. A bank's membership can be checked on the official website.
What is a transfer by phone number?
A transfer to the account linked to the recipient's number
The phone number serves as the account address. Before sending, check the recipient's name: the app shows it.
What is compounding of deposit interest?
Interest is added to the deposit and also earns income
With compounding, income grows faster: interest accrues both on the initial amount and on the interest already added.
A 100,000 ₽ deposit for a year at 12% with monthly compounding. Roughly how much at the end?
A bit more than without compounding.
(1 + 0.12/12)^12 ≈ 1.1268. Monthly compounding gives about 112,680 ₽, which is 680 ₽ more than without it.
What is the effective rate on a deposit?
A nominal 12% with monthly compounding gives an effective ~12.68%. Deposits are better compared by the effective rate.
What is the grace period on a credit card?
The period during which spending can be repaid without interest
If you repay the full amount before the grace period ends, no interest accrues. It usually does not cover cash withdrawals and transfers.
Why is withdrawing cash from a credit card usually unprofitable?
High fee and interest right away, with no grace period
The withdrawal fee is often 3–5% plus a minimum amount, and interest starts from day one.
A card with several accounts in different currencies
A card only for paying abroad
A purchase is debited from the account in the needed currency without conversion, if such an account exists. Convenient, but check the tariffs.
What is important to check before opening a deposit?
The color of the bank's logo
The rate, term, early withdrawal terms and participation in deposit insurance
A high rate can vanish on early withdrawal, and a bank outside the insurance system risks losing everything.
What is the minimum payment on a credit card?
The amount you must pay to avoid being overdue
The amount after which the debt disappears
It saves you from delinquency, not from interest.
The minimum payment is usually 3–10% of the debt. It saves you from being overdue but not from interest: the debt will take years to repay.
Which deposit rate protects money from losing value?
If a deposit pays 6% and prices rise 8%, purchasing power falls about 2% a year even though the amount grows.
A list of all account transactions for a period
A statement helps you track expenses and spot suspicious charges.
The rate is 10%. What is better: a one-year deposit with monthly compounding or with interest paid at the end?
Where does interest start working earlier?
Monthly compounding gives about 10.47% effective return versus 10% with payment at the end.
What is two-factor authentication in a banking app?
Logging in from two phones at once
Login confirmed by a second method, such as a code or biometrics
Even if the password is stolen, you cannot log in without the second factor. That is exactly why SMS codes must never be shared.
Bank A: 11% with monthly compounding. Bank B: 11.5% paid at the end of the year. Where is the annual income higher?
A's effective rate: (1 + 0.11/12)^12 − 1 ≈ 11.57%. That is slightly more than 11.5%, so bank A is better.
What usually happens to interest if a term deposit is closed early?
It is recalculated at a reduced rate, often almost to zero
It is moved to a credit card
Many term deposits, when closed early, are recalculated at the "on demand" rate of about 0.01%.
Why should you not keep more than the deposit insurance limit in one bank?
The amount above the limit may not be returned if the license is revoked
The bank will charge a double fee
Insurance covers deposits in one bank only up to the limit, totaled across all accounts. Large sums are wisely spread across banks.
Limit 100,000 ₽, grace period 50 days. You spent 40,000 ₽ and returned 30,000 ₽ before the grace period ended. What happens?
Interest will be charged: grace requires repaying the full amount
The bank will take 10,000 ₽ from your deposit
The benefit works with full repayment.
The grace period works only with full repayment. Otherwise interest is usually charged on the whole amount from the purchase dates.
What is the currency risk of keeping savings in a foreign currency?
The bank may refuse to exchange
The exchange rate may move against you
You spend in one currency and save in another.
If you spend in rubles but save in foreign currency, a stronger ruble will shrink your savings in rubles. Diversification reduces the risk.
What is the danger of linking many services to one main card without limits?
Auto-charges and leaks will affect all the money in the account
The bank will raise the deposit rate
For subscriptions and online purchases it is handy to have a separate card with a small balance or limit.
What is the central bank's key rate?
The rate at which the central bank lends to banks and takes their funds
The rate each bank sets itself
All other rates depend on it.
The key rate affects everything: when it rises, loans get more expensive and deposit rates rise; when it falls, the opposite.
A deposit at 9% a year, 13% tax on interest income (if it applies), inflation 8%. What is the approximate real return?
First subtract the tax from the rate.
After tax: 9% × 0.87 ≈ 7.83%. Minus 8% inflation, the real return is about −0.2%. The amount grows, but purchasing power does not.
credit: What is a loan interest rate?
The charge for using the bank's money, in percent per year
The amount of a late fine
The price of other people's money.
The rate shows how much it costs to use the bank's money for a year. But the real price of a loan is better seen in the full cost of credit.
A payment not made on time
Delinquency leads to fines, penalties and a worse credit history.
A list of banks in the country
Information on how you borrowed and repaid loans
It is kept by credit bureaus. Banks use it to decide whether to lend and at what rate.
Paying for a purchase in parts
An installment plan is essentially a loan. "0%" is often achieved through a seller discount, but there can be hidden fees and insurance.
Property the bank can take if the debt is not repaid
For a mortgage the collateral is usually the apartment itself, for a car loan the car.
A person responsible for the debt if the borrower does not pay
Becoming a guarantor is risky: someone else's debt can become yours.
Returning a loan ahead of schedule
Early repayment reduces the interest you overpay. It can usually be done without penalties if you notify the bank in advance.
A small short-term loan with a very high rate
Microloan rates, converted to a yearly basis, can be many times higher than bank rates. It is a last resort.
A housing loan secured by that housing
A mortgage is a long-term loan where the purchased home serves as collateral. The term is usually 10–30 years.
You realize you cannot make the next payment. What is best to do?
Take a microloan at a huge rate
Contact the bank in advance and discuss restructuring
Banks often meet you halfway: payment holidays, a longer term, a lower payment. Silence only worsens the situation.
What does the full cost of credit (APR) show?
All loan costs in percent per year, including fees and mandatory insurance
The full cost shows the real price of a loan. The rate may be 15% while the full cost is 22% because of insurance and fees. Compare loans by the full cost.
A payment that decreases every month
The same payment for the whole loan term
A one-time payment at the end
At the start of an annuity most of the payment goes to interest, toward the end to the principal.
Decreases: interest accrues on the remaining balance
The debt melts, and so does the payment.
The first payments are larger, but the total overpayment is lower than with an annuity.
A 100,000 ₽ loan for a year at 20% a year, annuity. Approximate overpayment?
The payment is ≈ 9,240 ₽, ≈ 110,900 ₽ per year. The overpayment is about 10,900 ₽, not 20,000: interest accrues on a shrinking balance.
A new loan on better terms to pay off the old one
Refinancing makes sense if the new rate is noticeably lower and switching fees are small.
Early payment: reduce the term or reduce the payment, which cuts the overpayment more?
Fewer months mean less interest accrued. Reducing the payment is easier on the budget, but the savings are smaller.
What are payment holidays on a loan?
A free vacation from the bank
A temporary deferral or reduction of loan payments
Payment holidays give a breather, but interest usually keeps accruing and the total term grows.
The share of income that goes to loan payments
How much of your income debts eat up.
If DTI is above 50%, the bank sees a high risk. For a borrower it is a signal not to take on new debts.
Why should an ad saying "loan with no refusals in 5 minutes" make you wary?
It is a sign of a reliable bank
Most likely a huge rate or a scam
That is how the central bank lends
Reliable lenders check your ability to pay. A promise without checks is a sign of expensive loans or a scam with "prepayment for processing".
You have never taken loans. What is your credit history like?
There is none, so banks find it harder to assess you
The state fines you for it
An empty history is not bad, just unknown. A credit card carefully repaid within the grace period can build it.
A "0%" installment plan for 30,000 ₽, but with mandatory insurance of 3,000 ₽. The real overpayment:
Add up everything you will pay.
Mandatory insurance and fees turn "0%" into a real overpayment. Look at the final amount in the contract.
The "avalanche" method: which debt to pay off first?
The one with the highest rate
The "avalanche" saves the most mathematically: the expensive debts stop growing first.
The rate is 15%, but the full cost with mandatory insurance is 21%. What does this mean?
The real cost of the loan is closer to 21% a year
The full cost includes everything mandatory.
The full cost includes all mandatory payments. It is the 21% you should compare with other banks' offers.
A 5 million ₽ mortgage for 20 years at 12%. What is the approximate total overpayment?
The payment is about 55 thousand a month.
The payment is ≈ 55 thousand ₽, ≈ 13.2 million ₽ over 20 years. The overpayment is larger than the loan itself, which is why early payments at the start of the term are so effective.
Why are early payments on an annuity better made at the start of the term?
The bank gives a bonus for them
At the start most of the payment is interest, and the savings are maximal
At the start of the term the payment is almost entirely interest. By reducing the debt early, you remove the interest for all the remaining years.
A mortgage with a floating rate
New loans are taken to pay old ones
Each new loan is more expensive than the previous one, and the debt grows. The way out is to stop new loans, make a repayment plan and ask the bank for restructuring.
A procedure to write off debts when you cannot pay, with serious consequences
Free write-off of any debts with no consequences
It is not a magic button.
Bankruptcy can free you from debts, but property will be sold to pay creditors, and for several years there will be restrictions on loans and some positions.
Credit card debt of 50,000 ₽ at 30%, you pay only the minimum 5% a month. What will happen?
The debt will be gone in 20 months without overpayment
The bank will forgive the rest
The debt will take years to repay with a big overpayment
The minimum shrinks along with the debt.
The minimum payment shrinks along with the debt, while interest eats a large part of it. Repayment stretches over years.
Why is a floating loan rate risky?
The payment can rise after the key rate
It is always higher than a fixed rate
A floating rate is tied to a market indicator. If rates in the economy rise, so does your payment.
Installments: 12 payments of 5,000 ₽, or pay 54,000 ₽ at once with a discount. You have the money. What is better?
Pay at once with the discount
Take a loan and pay at once
Installments will cost 60,000 ₽, paying at once 54,000 ₽. Even on a 10% deposit this money would bring less than 3,000 ₽ over the year on average. The discount is better.
